missions.what: Sub-group photo & video with the company banner (240 × 100 cm)
missions.how: The app is explicit: "Trip 12 — your Sub Group Photo spot is Ginzan Onsen on Day 3." Shoot on Shirogane Bridge in the first ten minutes of the 09:30 stop: it is Yamagata's officially designated viewpoint and the only level ground wide enough for 35 people, because the street itself is barely 4–5 m across with the river down the middle. Two rows of 17–18 along the bridge deck, front row holding the banner at hip height, photographer back on the road approach or the footbath apron. Light trap: the street runs on a bearing of about 153° and the sun sits at azimuth 132° at 09:30 rising to 152° by 10:30 — almost exactly down the street axis — so a camera pointing UP the street shoots into the sun. Either use fill flash, or reverse it and shoot down-street at 09:30–09:45 while the sun is lowest. Fallback if the bridge is jammed: the Shirogane Falls deck at the far end, near-empty in the morning, with a 22 m waterfall behind the banner — but the platform is tight, so plan two rows and a tighter crop.

missions.where: Day 4 hotel LOBBY, at dinner time — Ooedo Onsen Monogatari Premium Kinugawa Kanko Hotel
missions.how: Note the day: the app puts this on DAY 4, not Day 3. Solve the yukata before you solve the photograph, because at this hotel yukata are NOT left in the rooms — there is a free self-serve colour-yukata rack beside the front desk, in the lobby, and guests may wear them anywhere including the restaurant. With check-in 18:20 and dinner 18:30 that is a five-minute scramble, so e-mail a size split for all 35 ahead and ask for the sets to be pre-bagged — or better, ask for the group to take the 19:30 buffet sitting instead of 17:30, which buys a clean 18:40–19:15 window with the lobby half empty. Shoot with the front-desk wall and the self-playing grand piano behind you, NOT the entrance doors: after 18:00 the glass is black and backlighting 35 people will lose every face. Ask the duty manager the night before to hold a strip of lobby for ten minutes. Three rows of 12/12/11, tallest at the back on any step, shortest seated on lounge sofas in a shallow arc. Brief everyone that the yukata closes LEFT panel over right — right-over-left is for the dead — because a row of wrongly wrapped yukata is the one thing you cannot fix afterwards. Lock white balance around 3000–3200K rather than auto, and add one bounced LED from camera left. Fallbacks in order: the covered front entrance, which puts the hotel name in shot and works in rain; then Fureai Bridge, floodlit, 90 m away, but ask the hotel before taking 35 borrowed yukata outdoors.

missions.what: MAIN group photo & video with the banner — everyone
missions.how: On the Honmaru lawn, and take it FIRST, before anyone enters the keep. Split into 2–3 rows of about twelve; watch for wide-angle face distortion at the row ends. Stand the group 35–40 m out from the stone base with the camera another 12–15 m back on a 24–28 mm equivalent, so the five-tier red-tiled keep reads clear above the back row, and have two people hold the banner at knee height dead centre. Light is the trap again: the sun is at azimuth 219° and 51° altitude at 13:10, moving to 243° and 37° by 14:40 — south-west, directly behind the keep from the Honmaru. So work from the SOUTH-EAST corner looking WNW rather than from due east looking west, shoot at 13:15–13:35 rather than 14:20, and expose for faces with fill flash. Allow a genuine ten minutes just to form up 35 people, caps off, and post someone on a spare banner corner because the lawn catches a cross-breeze. Wet-weather fallback: the covered entrance hall of Tsurugajo Kaikan at the north gate, where the coach parks — the reconstructed castle corridor only shelters about fifteen.

missions.what: Official ViTrox social-media reel (vertical) — for all ViTroxians
missions.where: With the yukata — see the day conflict below
missions.how: Trips 1–10 shoot at airport departure and Trips 21–32 at Hitachi Seaside Park, but Trips 11–20 — including you — shoot in yukata. The videographer stands in the middle at about 2.5 m on a monopod at chest height, everyone turns to the front and says the trip number together. Shoot 9:16 vertical and run the beat twice, so the editor gets a clean second take, then grab a wide 16:9 still from the same position for the corporate deck. Shoot the reel FIRST, while the yukata are still crisp. Post to Instagram Stories mentioning @vitroxcorp with #ViTroxJapanTrip2026; selected stories get reposted by Corp Comm. CAUTION: the app contradicts itself on the day — the Mission 4 card says "Day3 with Yukata" while the Mission 2 card puts the yukata photo on Day 4. Since the yukata are at the Day 4 hotel, Day 4 is almost certainly right, but confirm with Ronald.

New in the app and not in the briefing PDF. Photographer: more than 5 photos per day, 35 minimum per trip. Videographer: 3 clips per day, 21 per trip. Ronald will contact the photographer about a week after the trip to collect everything. Full coverage entitles the photographer and videographer to 8 volunteer hours; each individual mission is worth 2.

x.contests: FY26 Q3 & Q4 ESP photo contest: each group photographer submits 10 photos across two categories, 5 each — Most Creative Group Photos and Most Stunning Scenery. Submission deadline 31 December 2026, winners announced 2027 Q1. Reward RM500 per category for five group winners, with an overall RM1,000 V-Wallet voucher. practical: Japan is 1 hour ahead of Malaysia — set your watch forward on landing.
100 V / 50 Hz, Type A and B flat two-pin sockets. Malaysian hair appliances rated 230 V may not work; check before packing.
Baggage: 25 kg checked, 7 kg hand-carry, one piece each, no single bag over 32 kg. Power banks in the cabin, maximum two, each under 20,000 mAh.
Clothing per the briefing: t-shirt, light jacket, umbrella. Add one light layer for the 09:20 Kegon Falls stop at 1,269 m and the two mountain onsen evenings.
Visa-free 90 days for Malaysian ePassport holders. Register on Visit Japan Web before departure — one QR now covers immigration and customs.
Tax-free is still deducted AT THE TILL for this trip: ¥5,000 minimum per store per day, passport at the register. Japan switches to airport refunds on 1 November 2026, after you are home.
The trip window contains no Japanese public holiday and finishes four days before Silver Week (19–23 Sep 2026), so no holiday crowds or pricing.

Full-board meals throughout, with pork-free, halal, vegetarian and special-dietary arrangements available — the app badges the vegetarian option on nearly every meal. Menus flex with seasonal availability.

The app has no live flight alerts for this trip: "Live delay/reschedule alerts aren't set up for this trip yet." September is Japan's peak typhoon-landfall month, so check JMA and the airline yourself from 48 hours out.
