items.name: Haneda Airport — Terminal 3
items.subtitle: 羽田空港 第3ターミナル
items.summary: SQ634 lands 21:55 at Haneda's international terminal, arrivals on 2F. The transfer to tonight's hotel is only about 1.3 km — the app says a 5-minute coach ride — which is the single best thing about this itinerary's opening. The app does not print terminal numbers; T3 is inferred from Singapore Airlines' international operation.

x.mustDo: Have the Visit Japan Web QR open before you reach the hall. One code now covers immigration and the customs declaration, and Haneda has the Electronic Customs Declaration gates that read it. Keep the group together at the 2F arrivals meeting point — at 22:00 the terminal empties fast.
x.mustEat: Nothing worth queueing for at 22:00 — the 4F and 5F Edo Koji restaurants have closed. The honest answers are the terminal konbini and the vending machines, and it is a five-minute ride to the hotel.
x.mustBuy: Do not shop here. You return to Narita Terminal 1 on Day 8 with roughly three hours to spare, and that is where the chilled and heavy things belong — Royce nama chocolate, Shiroi Koibito tins, anything needing an ice pack.
x.mustSee: The 5F Edo Koji mock-Edo street, with its wooden shopfronts and paper lanterns, is worth the two-minute detour even shuttered. The rooftop observation deck has closed by the time you land.

items.name: Hotel Metropolitan Haneda
items.subtitle: ホテルメトロポリタン羽田
items.summary: Night 1. Inside Haneda Innovation City, one minute from the HICity gate of Tenkubashi Station and one rail stop from Terminal 3. Book the coach both ways: the hotel's own free shuttle is airport-BOUND only (04:20–11:05) and the HICity airport loop runs 11:00–18:00, so there is no scheduled way IN from T3 at 22:30. The app shows no check-in time for tonight.

essentials.value: Haneda Innovation City Zone A, 1-1-4 Hanedakuko, Ota-ku, Tokyo

essentials.detail: Tuesday, arriving about 22:50–23:15 once bags are cleared. By then HICity's food hall (to 22:30), the brewery (to 23:00) and the sake bar (to 23:00) are shut or shutting. What genuinely still works: Matsuya round the clock, Daily Yamazaki until 23:00, the Ashiyu Sky Deck footbath until 23:30, and THE ROOFTOP all night. The hotel locks its street entrance overnight, so late walkers need their card key.

Breakfast at il CIELO HANEDA on 5F opens 06:00 (last entry 09:30), so the 07:30 sitting is comfortable and could even be pulled forward. That leaves a real pre-08:30 window: THE ROOFTOP is already open and the Ashiyu Sky Deck opens 05:30, both within 300 m, with sunrise about 05:19. The coach then leaves 08:30 for Tokyo Station — about 18 km and 45 minutes.

x.mustDo: THE ROOFTOP on the top floor — a 24-hour guests-only deck, card key required, taking in Terminal 3 and the runways, Tokyo Skytree, Tokyo Tower and the Rainbow Bridge. It is open all night and closed only in rain, which makes it the one thing that still works whatever time you get in.
x.mustEat: Matsuya at HICity Zone B 2F is open 24 hours, two minutes away — cheap gyudon and tonkatsu from a ticket machine, with a roughly 7% surcharge after 22:00. It is not halal and it is beef and pork, so treat it as a fallback for whoever is still hungry rather than a group plan.
x.mustBuy: Daily Yamazaki in the same block, about a minute from the lobby, has an in-store bakery — but it shuts at 23:00 on a weekday, so this is a 15-minute window, not an open-ended one. Say so on the coach before anyone unpacks.
x.mustSee: The Ashiyu Sky Deck on the Zone E rooftop, 300 m away: a free open-air FOOTBATH with an unobstructed, fence-free view straight down Haneda's B runway. Open until 23:30 — so if you move, you make it.

x.summary: Assemble at the Penang International Airport check-in counter by 07:00. SQ131 PEN 10:15 → Singapore 11:45, a 55-minute connection, then SQ634 SIN 13:55 → HANEDA 21:55 — about 20h 20m door to door. You land at Haneda and fly home from Narita, which is why the agent's sheets are headed "Narita / Haneda". Baggage is 25 kg checked and 7 kg hand-carry, one piece. Register on Visit Japan Web before you fly; Malaysian ePassport holders are visa-free for 90 days.
x.sun: Penang sunrise 07:15, Tokyo sunset 17:58 — but you are in the air for all of it. Landing 21:55 in full dark; the moon and the apron floodlights are your only light.
x.outfitPhoto: Only two frames today: the 07:00 assembly at the Penang check-in counter, and whatever anyone shoots from THE ROOFTOP at midnight. For the assembly, plain solid colours over busy prints — a 35-person line-up in patterns turns to visual noise at any distance. Note Trip 12 does NOT shoot the airport reel; that is Trips 1–10, so this is a casual record shot, not a mission.
x.outfitPractical: Twenty hours and twenty minutes door to door in a cabin held near 23°C, so a light long-sleeve layer beats a jacket you have to carry. Slip-on shoes for two security screenings. Malaysia to Japan is a 1-hour time change only, so no real jet lag — but you reach the room close to midnight and the coach leaves at 08:30.

legs.label: Day 1 — Terminal 3 to Haneda Innovation City, about 1.3 km and 5 minutes by coach. Book it: the hotel shuttle only runs the other way.

days.areaSpan: Haneda → Tokyo Station → Sendai → Matsushima → Naruko

items.name: Tokyo Station
items.subtitle: 東京駅
items.summary: 08:30 from the hotel, 09:15 arrival, 10:05 Shinkansen to Sendai (about 1h35). Fifty minutes in the station is comfortable — and the Haneda hotel is what makes it so, because 18 km from Tenkubashi works where 65 km from Narita would not have.

x.mustDo: Buy ekiben at Ekibenya Matsuri in Gransta Tokyo, on the 1F Central Passage inside the gates — over 150 varieties, open from 05:30, so it is trading when you arrive. Do this first, then look at the building.
x.mustEat: Gyuniku Domannaka (牛肉どまん中) by Shinkineya of Yonezawa, ¥1,620 — the perennial No.1 seller at Ekibenya Matsuri: soy-simmered Yonezawa beef with beef soboro over rice, and exactly the right thing to eat on a Tohoku Shinkansen.
x.mustBuy: At 09:15 the Gransta souvenir and cosmetics units are shut until 10:00, so buy from the bento and sweets counters: the caramel-butter (NO) RAISIN SANDWICH, 4 pieces ¥1,580, is a Tokyo-Station exclusive that travels well, and Tokyo Banana is sold inside the gates.
x.mustSee: The restored 1914 Marunouchi domes at the North and South gates — eight zodiac reliefs at the octagon's diagonal corners, and the four cardinal animals (rat, rabbit, horse, rooster) deliberately missing. Free, indoors, two minutes from the Central Passage.

items.name: Sendai Station
items.subtitle: 仙台駅
items.summary: Arrival 11:40, then about 40 minutes and 29 km by coach to Matsushima for a 12:15 lunch. This is a 20-minute grab-and-go, not a sit-down.

x.mustDo: Walk the 3F Gyutan-dori and Sushi-dori arcades directly above the Shinkansen gates — six beef-tongue specialists side by side, including Date no Gyutan Honpo, Aji no Gyutan Kisuke and Sumiyaki Rikyu.
x.mustEat: Zunda shake at Zunda Saryo's Zunda Komichi store on 3F — ¥420 short, ¥530 tall. A sweet green-soybean milkshake drunk in three minutes, and edamame is at its seasonal peak in early September.
x.mustBuy: Hagi no Tsuki (萩の月) by Kasho Sanzen, 6-piece box ¥1,590, from Omiyage-dokoro Sendai No.3 on 2F west, open 07:00–20:00. It keeps about 14 days, so it survives the flight; Kikufuku's zunda cream daifuku tastes better but ships frozen and will not.
x.mustSee: From the 2F West Exit pedestrian deck, straight down the zelkova avenue of Aoba-dori — the green tunnel that earns Sendai its name, Mori no Miyako, the City of Trees, and still fully leafed in September.
x.confidenceNote: The West Exit pedestrian deck has had recurring redevelopment hoardings; check the Aoba-dori sightline is open before routing 35 people onto it.

items.name: Matsushima Fish Market
items.subtitle: 松島さかな市場
items.summary: 13:18, one hour — and the app confirms the name is Matsushima, not Sendai, which settles a disagreement between the briefing's two slides. Run by the owners of six Kesennuma tuna longliners, so tuna is the September strength. Weekday hours 09:00–16:00 with food last orders around 15:00.

x.mustDo: Order at the 1F counter and eat standing. The next stop is 450 m and seven walking minutes away — that short transfer is exactly why this is the Matsushima market and not the one in central Sendai, 25 km back down the line.
x.mustEat: The kaki burger (かきバーガー), ¥380 — the market's own invention, a breaded oyster patty in a bun. It is cooked, which matters here: Miyagi's oyster season is a winter one and the grill hall upstairs does not really get going until November. A maguro-don from their own boats runs ¥750–2,400.
x.mustBuy: Kaki-shoyu (oyster soy sauce) and Sanriku Kaiho-zuke from the 1F souvenir wall — shelf-stable, cabin-bag friendly, and the honest way to take Matsushima oyster flavour home in September. Sanriku wakame is the other volume seller.
x.mustSee: Whole tuna and the collar and cheek cuts laid out on ice at the 1F counter, landed by the market's own Kesennuma fleet — and upstairs, the ranks of charcoal grills in the Yakigaki House standing idle, waiting for the season.
x.confidenceNote: The app bills today's lunch as "Oyster Set Cuisine", but the market itself flags November–March as the real oyster season and the date Miyagi opens raw-consumption shipping each year could not be confirmed — so expect a cooked or year-round preparation rather than fresh local raw oysters.

items.name: Zuiganji Temple
items.subtitle: 瑞巌寺
items.summary: 14:20, one hour — exactly right for the Hondo, the Kuri and the Seiryuden museum. April–September 08:30–17:00, last admission 16:30, with no closing days listed. Admission rose on 1 April 2026 to ¥1,000, but groups of 30 or more pay ¥900 each, so book as a group.

x.mustDo: Go slowly through the Hondo — a National Treasure completed in 1609 for Date Masamune, built with Kumano cedar and Kyoto craftsmen — then finish in the Seiryuden treasure museum, which is inside the same ticket.
x.mustEat: Zunda shake, ¥360, at Kasho Sanzen's Matsushima Teramachi-Koji store on the lane between the temple and Matsushima-Kaigan Station, 09:00–18:00 — the one quick cold thing on the approach that works for 35 people.
x.mustBuy: The Zuiganji goshuin at ¥500, or the temple's own seal book at ¥1,200, from the desk by the Kuri exit — the only souvenir here that is actually Zuiganji rather than generic Matsushima.
x.mustSee: The Shitchu "Peacock Room" in the Hondo, its gold-leaf sliding doors painted with peacocks and pines, showpiece of the 2008–2018 restoration — and on the way in, the tuff cave tombs cut into the cliff along the approach, packed with weathered Buddhas.

items.name: Godaido Hall
items.subtitle: 五大堂
items.summary: 15:22, thirty minutes, free, no closing day. Access shuts at dusk. Bridge repairs have always been scheduled in winter, so there is no September risk.

x.mustDo: Cross the two vermilion sukashibashi — the lattice-floored bridges that show the sea five metres below through the gaps, built so pilgrims had to watch their step and compose themselves. Warn anyone in heels; wheelchairs cannot manage the lattice.
x.mustEat: Gyutan korokke, ¥350, at Genzo (げんぞう) literally at the entrance, 10:30–16:30. Or Pensee Matsushima's oyster curry bread at ¥300 — a 2020 Curry Bread Grand Prix gold winner and the smart September oyster fix, because it is fried rather than raw.
x.mustBuy: Sasakamaboko from Matsushima Kamaboko Honpo Sohonten, 09:00–17:00, never closed — and if there is time, the ¥300 hand-grilling counter where you toast your own over charcoal.
x.mustSee: From the seaward side, the classic Matsushima composition: pine-topped islets, the vermilion Fukuura bridge to the left, cruise boats crossing. Then look up under the eaves — the twelve zodiac animals are carved on the four faces, each at its compass direction.

items.name: Matsushima Bay Cruise — Nioumaru course
items.subtitle: 松島湾遊覧船（仁王丸コース）
items.summary: 16:00, a 50-minute loop from the central pier two minutes from Godaido. Critical: sailings are hourly from 09:00 and 16:00 is the LAST boat of the day, so a late coach means no cruise at all. Have the guide hold the tickets and board by 15:50.

x.mustDo: Board the Nioumaru. Base fare ¥1,500 adult, ¥750 child; groups of 15 or more get 10% off the adult fare, so ask.
x.mustEat: Gyutan skewers at Matsushima Kushiya, directly opposite the pier, 10:00–17:00 — buy before boarding, because the shop shuts soon after the last cruise returns around 16:50 and the boat's own catering is minimal.
x.mustBuy: The 2F Green-seat upgrade: +¥600 adult, +¥300 child. For a group photographing islands it is the only purchase that changes the experience — open-air upper deck instead of a glassed-in cabin.
x.mustSee: Nio-jima, the wave-cut rock the course is named for, said to look like a temple guardian smoking a pipe, and Kanejima, pierced by four surf-cut caves. The loop also passes Senganjima, Futagojima, Yoroijima, Kabutojima and Ojima.
x.confidenceNote: Sailings are cancelled in rough weather and September is peak typhoon month — hold a fallback (the Zuiganji museum, or Entsuin at ¥500) for a scrubbed 16:00 departure. Feeding the gulls from the deck has been discontinued, so do not promise it.

items.name: Hotel Kameya, Naruko Onsen
items.subtitle: ホテル亀屋
items.summary: Night 2, and the only hotel both source documents agreed on from the start. Check-in 18:30 after a 66 km, 1h30 run up from Matsushima; kaiseki dinner 19:00. Naruko sits around 200 m in a gorge and holds 9 of Japan's 11 recognised spring types, which is the fact worth telling the group before they get in.

essentials.detail: Wednesday. Taki-no-Yu, the cypress bath with pH2.9 sulphur water, runs 07:30–21:00 (last entry 20:30) for ¥300; Waseda Sajiki-yu is the latest at 09:00–21:30 for ¥660. Two free footbaths sit by the station, always open. Bring your own soap and towel — Taki-no-Yu sells neither.

Bittersweet timing: the 71st All-Japan Kokeshi Festival and the 35th Naruko Lacquerware Exhibition ran 5–6 September, three days before you arrive, so the town will be quiet with the banners still up. Dawn steam-walk from Yumeguri Hiroba, breakfast 07:30, coach 08:30.

x.mustDo: Bathe in Kameya's black water (黒湯) across all three baths — the valley-view tenbo daiyokujo, the hinoki cypress bath and the source-fed rotenburo.
x.mustEat: Tonight is the hotel kaiseki. Tomorrow morning, kuri-dango at Mochidokoro Fukase by the station — a whole syrup-steeped chestnut inside mochi under sweet walnut-miso sauce, ¥400 for two, the same recipe for over a century — but it opens 09:00, so it needs the guide to agree a stop.
x.mustBuy: A Naruko kokeshi from Sakurai Kokeshi-ten honten, three minutes from the station — weekdays 10:00–17:00, workshop behind the counter. Naruko kokeshi are the ones that squeak when you turn the head, and the Naruko style is the most collected of the eleven traditional lineages.
x.mustSee: The steam. Naruko vents sulphurous steam from roadside sources, and the best free vantage is the stone stairway up to Naruko Onsen Shrine above Taki-no-Yu, looking back down over the tin roofs. Do not promise autumn colour — Naruko-kyo gorge peaks late October.
x.confidenceNote: Hotel Kameya's own bath hours, and whether its complimentary Taki-no-Yu ticket applies to a group tour rate, could not be confirmed — ask when reconfirming the 18:30 check-in. This is also the one hotel whose address the app does not expose (its map link is a shortened URL with no address text).

x.summary: Coach 18 km to Tokyo Station, then the Tohoku Shinkansen 304 km north to Sendai and the Matsushima Bay circuit — one of Japan's three classic views. Wednesday 9 September is not a public holiday and nothing on today's list takes a Wednesday off. The 16:00 bay cruise is the LAST sailing of the day, so the whole afternoon hinges on it.
x.sun: Sunrise 05:12, sunset 17:54 at Matsushima. The afternoon sun swings from SW (az 222°, alt 49°) at the fish market to due W (az 259°, alt 22°) by the 16:00 cruise — so the bay is progressively back-lit as the day goes on.
x.outfitPhoto: The Matsushima palette is blue-grey sea, near-black pine islets and VERMILION bridges. That makes two colours risky: dark green disappears into the pines, and orange or red fights the vermilion of the Fukuura and Godaido bridges, which is the one colour every photo here is built around. Mid-tone blue, navy or a soft neutral reads cleanly against both sea and pine. White works against the dark islets but blows out under a 49° sun at 13:18.
x.outfitPractical: Matsushima is 29°/22° and coastal, so a sea breeze makes it feel kinder than inland — until 16:00, when the open 2F cruise deck is genuinely windy and carries spray. The three afternoon stops are 450 m, 500 m and 280 m apart on flat paving, so this is an easy walking day. The exception is Godaido: its two bridges have lattice floors that show the sea five metres below through the gaps, so no heels and no open-toe, and they cannot take a wheelchair.

legs.label: Day 2 — Haneda Innovation City to Tokyo Station, 08:30–09:15, about 18 km and 45 minutes by coach
Tohoku Shinkansen — Tokyo to Sendai, 10:05–11:40, about 304 km via Omiya, Utsunomiya and Fukushima
Day 2 by coach — Sendai to the Matsushima circuit (29 km), then 66 km northwest and 1h30 up to Naruko Onsen

items.name: Ginzan Onsen Street
items.subtitle: 銀山温泉
items.summary: 09:30–11:30. TRIP 12'S SUB-GROUP BANNER PHOTO IS HERE — the app confirms it: "Trip 12 — your Sub Group Photo spot is Ginzan Onsen on Day 3." Shoot it in the first ten minutes on Shirogane Bridge; 09:30–10:00 is the quietest the bridge will be all day, and by 11:00 the day-trip coaches make it the worst choke point on the street.

x.mustDo: Photo first, then walk the whole 400 m car-free street on the right bank and continue five minutes to Shirogane Falls in Shirogane Park. Free footbath Waraku Ashiyu (06:00–22:00) by the river at the entrance for the regroup.
x.mustEat: Standing-eat thick fried tofu (立ち食い生あげ) at Nogawa Toufuya, ¥250, cash only, 07:30 to about 15:00 or sold out. Second bite: Haikara-san no Curry Pan, about ¥250 — the original shop has closed for relocation, so it is now sold at Kashidokoro Meiyu-an right beside Shirogane Bridge, 08:00–17:30.
x.mustBuy: Karinto-manju at Meiyu-an — ¥130 each or ¥790 for a box of six, shelf-stable and ideal for carrying back to Malaysia. Yagihashi Shoten on the street pours Yamagata jizake tastings from ¥500 and sells Yamakawa Mitsuo and Tatenokawa by the bottle.
x.mustSee: From the middle of Shirogane Bridge: the double row of three- and four-storey wooden ryokan facing each other across the Ginzan river, with Notoya Ryokan's kote-e plasterwork facade and rooftop lookout tower on the right. At the far end, Shirogane Falls drops 22 m and splits in two, with a deck close enough to feel the spray.
x.confidenceNote: Coach access needs confirming. Tour coaches and charter taxis are excluded from the street itself and transfer at the Taisho Roman-kan lot (10 coach bays, free, 08:30–17:30), which reads as standing policy. The separate park-and-ride restriction is a WINTER measure — it ran 20 Dec 2025 to 1 Mar 2026 at ¥1,000–1,500 per person return, has ended, and no 2026-27 period has been announced — so it should not apply on 10 September, but do not assume either way. Call the info centre on 0237-28-3933. Also: Wamoyou is closed Thursdays, and no tamagoyaki shop or tofu ice cream could be found on the street despite common claims.

items.name: Zao Fox Village
items.subtitle: 蔵王キツネ村
items.summary: The app prints 15:10–16:40, but the park CLOSES at 16:30 in summer (last admission 16:00), so the real stop is 80 minutes, not 90 — worth raising with the agent. Closed every Wednesday, with exceptions in February, August, the May holidays and on national holidays, so Thursday 10 September is a normal open day. Admission ¥1,500, cash.

x.mustDo: Walk the free-roam enclosure circuit twice — once high, once low — because the foxes move with the sun. Brief the group at the gate on the rules that get enforced: keep walking, never crouch or sit down to fox level, remove every dangling strap and charm from bags, carry no food or drink in your hands, do not reach out to touch a roaming fox. They bite.
x.mustEat: Nothing — this is a genuine no-eating stop. There is no restaurant and food is banned in the enclosure because the foxes will lunge for it. If the coach pulls out by about 16:15, the soft-serve at Zao Dairy Centre's Cheese House is the nearest pairing; otherwise dinner is the answer.
x.mustBuy: Fox goods at the entrance shop by reception, which takes cards even though admission does not. The plush fox is the group-friendly buy — but note the shop also stocks real fur, which some colleagues will not want, and photography inside the shop is banned.
x.mustSee: From the upper path, looking down into the hollow where dozens of foxes lie out in the afternoon sun. The gradient is the whole point: it lets you shoot down at eye level without crouching, which is forbidden. Photography is prohibited at the enclosure entrance, at the caged and resting foxes, in the holding room, in the small-animal section and in the shop.
x.confidenceNote: Set expectations before the coach arrives: in September the foxes are in thin, patchy moulting coat, nothing like the winter fluff online, and the animal odour is strongest in heat. The fox-holding experience is widely reported to run only at 11:00 and 14:00, and feeding (¥200) to be weekends and holidays only, but neither is stated on the village's own site — if the 11:00/14:00 pattern holds, a 15:10 arrival misses both, and 35 people could not be put through one round anyway. Ring 0224-24-8812.

items.name: Okuiizaka Anabara Onsen Yoshikawaya
items.subtitle: 奥飯坂 穴原温泉 吉川屋
items.summary: Night 3, check-in 17:45, kaiseki dinner 18:00. Founded in 1841, four wings, step-free throughout, and 150 parking spaces that take coaches. Anabara is NOT part of Iizaka Onsen — it is a quiet six-ryokan pocket 2 km upstream on the Surikami river, with one public bath and no shopping street. Set expectations accordingly.

essentials.detail: Thursday, and quiet. After the 18:00 kaiseki there is no lit street outside the door — the evening is the river, the hotel's own open-airs until midnight, and Tennoji Anabara-yu, Anabara's only public bath, 300 m away (¥400, Thursdays 13:00–21:00, last entry 20:40). The book lounge with 4,000 manga titles runs to 23:00 for anyone who does not bathe. For Iizaka's lit bridge or the gyoza it is a 5-minute taxi each way — the hotel shuttle stops at 18:00, so book returns before dinner.

Baths reopen 05:00 with the sides swapped, so early risers get the pair they missed. Better still, Tennoji Anabara-yu opens at 06:00 on Fridays, so a three-minute walk and ¥400 buys a genuine local public bath before the 07:30 breakfast buffet and the 08:30 coach.

x.mustDo: Soak the two riverside open-air baths, Saruami-no-Yu and Kamoshika-no-Yu, straight over the Surikami rapids — 14:00–24:00 and 05:00–10:00, with the men's and women's sides swapping between evening and morning, so you get both. The hotel markets these as Fukushima's largest bath-and-rotenburo complex.
x.mustEat: The kaiseki centres on Fukushima beef grilled on a ceramic plate with a fruit-based sauce. If anyone gets out to Iizaka, the city's signature dish is enban gyoza — a whole disc of 22 gyoza flipped out onto the plate — at Gyoza no Terui's Iizaka branch, ¥1,200, 17:00–21:00 or until sold out, closed Wednesdays so open tonight.
x.mustBuy: Radium eggs (ラヂウム玉子) from Aberu Shoten, 08:00–19:00, closed Tuesdays, two minutes from Iizaka Onsen Station — a Taisho-era accident where eggs left in the spring came out with the white still runny, and a doctor's remark about radium in the water gave them the name. Fukushima peaches are still on until about mid-September.
x.mustSee: The Surikami gorge directly below the hotel's open-air baths — the best view on the property and free. In Iizaka itself, Totsuna-bashi: a 51.7 m steel arch bridge of 1915, one of the oldest surviving Taisho arch bridges, floodlit every night since 2009, and the single best photograph in the area.
x.confidenceNote: Coordinates are the mean of two independent listings agreeing to about 30 m, and sit 230 m west of Fukushima City's own coordinate for the Anabara public bath, which is the correct geometry. Two things to confirm in writing: a 35-person group will normally be put in a banquet hall rather than the private rooms, and plain ryokan yukata are provided — there is no colour-yukata selection service here, so do not promise one.

x.summary: Cross into Yamagata for the Taisho-era onsen street, then 130 km south for the foxes, and over into Fukushima for the night. TRIP 12'S SUB-GROUP BANNER PHOTO IS AT GINZAN ONSEN TODAY. Ginzan in September is deep green and lush — not the snow scene the postcards sell.
x.sun: Sunrise 05:15, sunset 17:54. At the 09:35 photo the sun is SE at az 133°, alt 47°, moving to SSE az 152° by 10:30 — and Ginzan's street runs on a bearing of about 153°, so the sun sits almost exactly down the street axis all morning.
x.outfitPhoto: TODAY IS THE SUB-GROUP BANNER PHOTO, so this matters more than any other day. September Ginzan is a wall of deep green foliage, weathered dark-brown timber and a grey-green river — which means GREEN, BEIGE, BROWN AND OLIVE all disappear into the background. What lifts off it: white, cream, pale blue, and any clear mid-tone. Coordinate one thing with the photographer: the front row should not match the banner, or the banner stops reading. Because the sun runs down the street axis, shooting UP-street is straight into it — shoot down-street at 09:30–09:45 while the sun is lowest, or use fill flash.
x.outfitPractical: Ginzan's 400 m street is car-free and flat, with a five-minute path on to Shirogane Falls that stays damp. Zao Fox Village is the day's real constraint: gravel and dirt on a slope, foxes roaming loose, and a rule set that is actually enforced — keep walking, never crouch or sit to fox level, no food or drink in your hands, and remove everything that dangles. Long trousers and closed shoes. September is moulting season, so the animals are patchy and the smell is strong in the heat; it gets into fabric.

legs.label: Day 3 by coach — Naruko to Ginzan Onsen (44 km, 56 min), then 130 km and 2h10 south to Zao Fox Village, and 45 km / 1h05 over into Fukushima for Anabara Onsen

items.name: Goshikinuma Ponds
items.subtitle: 五色沼
items.summary: 10:00–11:00 after a 68 km, 1h30 run. Be realistic: from the east trailhead beside the Urabandai Visitor Centre, 60 minutes buys Bishamon-numa and little else — the full trail is 3.6–4 km and 90 minutes one way. Free 24-hour toilets and a 92-space car park at the trailhead.

x.mustDo: Walk the paved barrier-free path to the Bishamon-numa deck and rowboat pier, about five minutes in, then take the north-shore boardwalk for two or three more viewpoints. If the guide wants three of the bluest ponds in the same hour, drop the coach at the WEST end instead — Yanagi-numa is four minutes in, then Ao-numa, Ruri-numa and Benten-numa.
x.mustEat: The emerald-green "Goshikinuma" soft-serve from the kiosk by the trailhead car park — bright turquoise, not matcha, and the standard group photo prop. Today's 12:00 lunch is unnamed in the app and the transfer clock puts it on the Inawashiro corridor, where the local plates are Aizu sauce katsudon and Aizu-jidori chicken, which received Geographical Indication protection in March 2025.
x.mustBuy: Aizu yama-shio (会津山塩), salt boiled down from the Oshio Urabandai hot-spring brine, about ¥450 a bag from Urabandai Bussankan at the west end. Be honest with the group: the east trailhead plaza sells only maps and postcards, and the visitor centre has no shop at all.
x.mustSee: Bishamon-numa — the largest of the twenty-odd ponds, cobalt-emerald from dissolved volcanic minerals, with the blown-out crater wall of Mt Bandai rising straight behind it from the first deck. Have the group hunt the heart-marked carp in the shallows; it keeps 35 people happy for ten minutes.

items.name: Tsuruga Castle (Tsurugajo)
items.subtitle: 鶴ヶ城
items.summary: 13:10–14:40. TRIP 12'S MAIN GROUP PHOTO WITH THE BANNER IS HERE — the app lists it as Mission 3, Day 4. Shoot it FIRST, before entering the keep. Hours 08:30–17:00, last entry 16:30, no closing days. Admission ¥410 adult individually, ¥520 with the Rinkaku tea house — but ¥360 each for groups of 30–99, so book as a group.

x.mustDo: Photo, then the keep: five floors of local-history museum, the Tetsumon gate where Matsudaira Katamori directed the 1868 Boshin War defence, the reconstructed Minamihashiri-Nagaya and Hoshi-yagura built with Edo techniques, the 5F observation deck over the whole Aizu basin, and Rinkaku, the tea house rescued for Sen no Rikyu's son.
x.mustEat: Inside the park, Rinkaku serves matcha with a jouyo-manju of grated yam and rice flour for ¥600, orders to 16:00 — the calm option for a sub-group. Tsurugajo Kaikan at the north gate, where the coach parks, does Aizu sauce katsudon and wappa-meshi. Ask the guide to explain kozuyu, Aizu's ceremonial dried-scallop soup served in a shallow lacquer dish.
x.mustBuy: Tsurugajo Kaikan claims the prefecture's largest souvenir range and has 20 coach bays: akabeko, the nodding red papier-mâché cow charm against illness; okiagari-koboshi, the thumb-sized self-righting doll (tradition is one per family member plus a spare); and Aizu lacquerware. Named sake: Suehiro, Aizu Homare, Sharaku from Miyaizumi next to the castle. Skip awamanju — two-day shelf life, eat it, do not pack it.
x.mustSee: The keep itself — five tiers roofed in red akagawara tiles relaid in 2011, the only red-tiled keep in Japan. Then walk out over the Rokabashi covered bridge, rebuilt in 2018, and look down on the tallest of the fan-sloped ogi-no-kobai stone walls.

items.name: Ouchi-juku
items.subtitle: 大内宿
items.summary: 14:40–16:40. The village is free and always open, but the shops are people's houses and most trade only 09:00–16:00 — soba kitchens wind down from 15:30 and the street visibly empties by 16:30. Put eating at the FRONT of the slot and the viewpoint at the end.

x.mustDo: Walk the full 500 m of thatch — about 40 kayabuki farmhouses, a national Important Preservation District since 1981 — then climb the steps to the Miharashidai lookout behind Koyasu Kannon, free and always open, the only place you get the whole double row in one frame. Budget 20–25 minutes for the climb and the shot.
x.mustEat: Takato soba / negi soba — chilled soba eaten using a whole raw spring onion as chopsticks, biting the onion as you go for the wasabi-like kick. The famous house is Misawaya (¥1,500, 09:30–16:00, usually closed Wednesdays) in a 350-year-old farmhouse, which also does kozuyu at ¥600. Yamagataya does the same dish for ¥1,250, cash only. Add stick-grilled iwana char (about ¥550 at Man'ya) and shingoro mochi — pounded rice on a skewer under perilla-miso, charcoal-grilled — at Ajidokoro Minatoya.
x.mustBuy: The village's own preserves and crafts rather than mass-market souvenirs: nishin no sansho-zuke (herring cured with sansho pepper) boxed to take away, junen miso, yama-shio, tochi-no-mi horse-chestnut sweets, and hand-grilled senbei from Yamagataya. Buy before 16:00 — several tills close before the street does.
x.mustSee: The unbroken double line of thatch with the open water channel running down both sides, seen from the Miharashidai looking south. Your slot is the best light of the whole trip: the sun drops from 37° to 14° between 14:40 and 16:40, so you get raking side light and then genuinely golden light from about 16:00.
x.confidenceNote: Kintaro Soba Yamamotoya is closed Thursdays AND Fridays, so it will be shut on 11 September; Misawaya's Wednesday closure does not affect you. Shop closures here are irregular — ask the Ouchi-juku tourism association (0241-68-3611) for the September 2026 shop calendar nearer the date. Also: new-crop soba does not arrive until late October, so the soba you eat is last season's.

items.name: Ooedo Onsen Monogatari Premium Kinugawa Kanko Hotel
items.subtitle: 大江戸温泉物語Premium 鬼怒川観光ホテル
items.summary: Night 4, check-in 18:20, buffet dinner 18:30. THE YUKATA GROUP PHOTO AND THE OFFICIAL ViTrox REEL HAPPEN IN THIS LOBBY, at dinner time, in hotel-provided yukata. 172 rooms, upgraded to "Premium" in July 2024, ten baths of which six are open-air. The coach drops at the front door then parks off-site, so fix the pick-up point for 08:30.

essentials.detail: Friday, and tight: 18:20 arrival with dinner at 18:30 in a hotel where the yukata are collected in the lobby rather than found in the room. Run the lobby as one station — keys and yukata in the same lap, then the photo and reel, then the buffet. Afterwards the free Premium Lounge in the same room pours coffee, soft drinks and alcohol until 22:00, with karaoke, table tennis and the game corner to midnight and the baths to 24:00. Nothing commercial in Kinugawa is open after 20:00.

Baths reopen 05:00 with the sexes swapped; breakfast 07:30, coach 08:30 for Kegon Falls. The only outdoor window is 05:30–07:15, and it is a good one: Fureai Bridge is two minutes from the door and empty at dawn, and Takimi Bridge is a 17-minute walk for the ruins panorama in flat morning light — with a coach bay beside it, so it also works as a ten-minute stop on the way out.

x.mustDo: Pick a colour yukata off the free self-serve rack beside the front desk the moment you check in — that is the detail that makes the lobby shoot work here, because yukata are NOT left in the rooms. Then the baths: two complexes plus a rotating half-open-air, 15:00–24:00 and 05:00–10:00, gender-swapped between evening and morning.
x.mustEat: The buffet in Restaurant IWATO, off a 14-metre live kitchen. Named local items on the line: Utsunomiya gyoza, Tochigi nira soba (garlic-chive soba), Nasu chicken yurinchi, kuroge wagyu sukiyaki, market-direct sashimi and sushi, grilled unagi. Breakfast's signature is nokke-don, a build-your-own seafood rice bowl. It is a Japanese hotel buffet with pork on the line and no halal certification — tell the hotel a week ahead if anyone needs pork-free plates.
x.mustBuy: The lobby shop, conveniently the same lap of the room as the yukata rack: dried Nikko yuba, Tochiotome strawberry sweets, frozen Utsunomiya gyoza, Nikko Jingoro senbei, and Kinuta mascot goods. The Ooedo colour yukata is rental only and not for sale — say so before someone tries to pack one.
x.mustSee: The Kinugawa gorge from the hotel's own open-air baths, and from Fureai Bridge 90 m from the door — a pedestrian truss bridge with giant oni murals on its stair walls, floodlit at night. Then the thing Kinugawa is quietly famous for: a line of derelict riverside hotels on the east bank, best seen in one sweep from Takimi Bridge, 1.3 km north. One of them, the east annexe, shares this hotel's name and closed in 2008.
x.confidenceNote: The published buffet sittings are 17:30 and 19:30, ninety minutes each, allocated at check-in, with up to six staggered starts in peak season — so an 18:30 start for 35 people is a special group sitting and must be confirmed in writing. If the group is actually placed on 19:30, the whole yukata-photo schedule shifts. No lobby floor plan is published anywhere, so ask the hotel for a 館内図 and have someone check the space on arrival.

x.summary: West through the Bandai highlands into Aizu — volcanic ponds, a red-tiled castle keep, a thatched Edo post town — then 80 km south into Tochigi. TODAY CARRIES TWO PHOTO MISSIONS: the MAIN group photo with the banner at Tsuruga Castle, and the YUKATA group photo and reel in tonight's hotel lobby. The Aizu Autumn Festival is 19–20 September, so no clash.
x.sun: Sunrise 05:19, sunset 17:54. At the 13:15 main group photo the sun is SW at az 220°, alt 50°, moving to WSW az 243°, alt 37° by 14:40. At Ouchi-juku it drops to az 265°, alt 14° by 16:40 — genuinely golden.
x.outfitPhoto: TWO MISSIONS TODAY, and they want opposite things. Tsuruga Castle is white plaster, GREY stone and a RED tiled roof over a green lawn: red and maroon clash with the roof, and dark green sinks into the lawn, so white, cream, navy and pale blue are the safe picks — and light clothing genuinely helps, because from the Honmaru the keep is back-lit with the sun behind it at 220°. Shoot from the SOUTH-EAST corner looking WNW rather than from due east, take it at 13:15–13:35 rather than 14:20, and expose for faces with fill flash. The evening yukata photo needs nothing from your wardrobe — the hotel provides the yukata — but wear something you can change out of in five minutes.
x.outfitPractical: Goshikinuma at 820 m is the coolest stop, 22–25°C, but humid, with muddy boardwalk after rain and mosquitoes and horseflies still active in September. Then the Aizu basin: 28–30°C at about 79% humidity, and the Honmaru lawn is almost entirely unshaded — fill water bottles before the photo. Ouchi-juku is unshaded gravel, and the Miharashidai lookout is a genuine 20–25 minute round trip up steps that get slippery.

legs.label: Day 4 by coach — Anabara to Goshikinuma (68 km, 1h30), the unnamed 12:00 lunch on the Inawashiro corridor, Aizu-Wakamatsu (45 km), Ouchi-juku (30 km, 50 min), then 80 km and 1h40 south to Kinugawa Onsen

days.areaSpan: Kinugawa → Kegon Falls → Nikko → Edo Wonderland → Tsukuba

items.name: Kegon Falls
items.subtitle: 華厳の滝
items.summary: 09:20–10:20 after a 41 km, 50-minute climb. The elevator runs 07:30–18:00 in May–September with no closing day, so a 09:20 arrival is well inside opening and — being first thing on a Saturday — ahead of the queue that would eat this hour later in the day. IMPORTANT: the Akechidaira Ropeway shut for renovation after 15 January 2026, with reopening only "planned for September 2027", so the classic panorama of falls, lake and Mt Nantai is NOT available on this trip.

x.mustDo: Ride the Kegon Falls Elevator 100 m straight down through the bedrock — a one-minute ride, then about 70 steps out to the observation platform at basin level. Reported fares are ¥600 adult and ¥550 for groups of 30 or more, but see the flag. Also walk the FREE upper observation area behind the first car park, two minutes from the coach, which looks down on the falls and is your fallback if the lift queue builds.
x.mustEat: At 09:20 almost nothing up here is open yet — Juichiya does yuba yakisoba for ¥500 from 08:00, and Chuzenji Kanko Center opens 09:00 with counters of Nikko yuba at ¥650 and tamari pickles from ¥680. The hand-cut soba house does not open until 11:00, so it is out.
x.mustBuy: Rakusan Koji Kojimaya (09:00–20:00) sells its own "Rakusan-ko" wine aged five years in caves under Mt Nantai — ¥1,500 half-size, ¥2,500 full — and Nikko Gokenin sake at ¥2,250 for 1.8 L. Miyamado (09:00–17:00) does additive-free Kekko manju with Tokachi azuki from ¥1,500 for ten.
x.mustSee: The 97 m single drop, only about 7 m wide at normal flow, head-on from the basin platform with the Junitaki side-seeps trickling out of the cliff beside it. On a windy day the spray carries roughly 150 m to the deck and throws rainbows — and a 09:20 slot puts the morning sun behind you rather than in the lens.
x.confidenceNote: Water volume is dam-regulated and cuts both ways in September: after heavy rain the falls are spectacular (55 t/s during the October 2018 typhoon against a 1–2.5 t/s norm), but after a dry spell release drops to 0.1–0.3 t/s and the drop looks thin. Tochigi Prefecture publishes the live figure online — check the morning of. The lift fares could not be verified from the operator's own site, which publishes neither hours nor prices.

items.name: Nikko Toshogu Shrine
items.subtitle: 日光東照宮
items.summary: 11:00–12:15, and it is tight. Guides normally budget 1.5–2 hours and the published "short" route is 1–1.5, so on a Saturday at midday — the busiest hour of the busiest day — you will have to drop either the 207 steps to the Okumiya or the Naki-ryu queue. Decide before you start. Open 09:00–17:00 April–October, last entry 16:30, no closing day. Admission ¥1,600, and the group rate of ¥1,440 kicks in at exactly 35 people — a coach of 34 loses it.

x.mustDo: Work the standard order: Omotemon, the Sanzaru "see/hear/speak no evil" monkeys on the sacred stable, the Yomeimon whose Heisei restoration finished in March 2017, the Karamon and Honsha, then the Nemuri-neko sleeping cat above the Sakashitamon. Finish at the Honjido for the Naki-ryu, where a priest strikes wooden clappers under the dragon's head and only there does the ceiling produce the flutter-echo "cry" — Japanese commentary only, no photography, and it IS covered by the main ticket.
x.mustEat: Nikko yuba — spelled 湯波 here, thicker and rolled, not Kyoto's 湯葉. Ganso Nikko Yuba Ryori Ebisuya does courses ¥2,400–5,000, Yugen does yuba sets ¥1,590–2,130. Today's 12:30 lunch is a ramen and gyoza set, so the yuba is a thing to seek out rather than the meal. Deep-fried yuba manju, ¥300, at Sakaeya — but the shop is outside Tobu Nikko Station, 1.3 km below Shinkyo bridge, not at the bridge.
x.mustBuy: Goshuin are all pre-written slips at ¥500 (no on-the-spot brushwork), so waits are usually under ten minutes — collect at the office just inside the Yomeimon and at the Yakushido exit for the Naki-ryu stamp. Then Kanaya Hotel Bakery for the cheese bread and the traditional rusks, from the Shinkyo branch or the hotel gift shop (08:00–18:00); the retort hyakunen curry is about ¥1,100 a box.
x.mustSee: The Yomeimon at close range — some 500 carvings of Chinese sages, dragons and children across 11 m of gate, which is why it is nicknamed the sunset gate: you could look at it until dusk. The Sanzaru panel is one scene in an eight-panel monkey life-cycle frieze, and its faces were noticeably repainted in 2017, a detail Japanese visitors still argue about.

items.name: Edo Wonderland Nikko Edomura
items.subtitle: 江戸ワンダーランド 日光江戸村
items.summary: 14:00–16:30, two and a half hours. Open 09:00–17:00 from 20 March to 30 November, with in-village entry closing at 16:00 — so a 14:00 arrival is fine but the slot runs right to the wire. Closed every WEDNESDAY, so Saturday 12 September is a normal operating day.

x.mustDo: Grab the printed show timetable at the gate the moment you enter. In 2.5 hours you can realistically do the Ninja Trick Maze and the tilted-floor Ninja Karakuri Mansion plus two or three shows — pick from the Ninja Theatre, the Mizugei-za water-magic illusion show, and the Minami-machi Bugyosho courtroom comedy. Costume rental starts at ¥2,800 and takes 30–45 minutes to dress, so it costs you a show.
x.mustEat: Named counters on the street: Nihon-soba Yabu (¥900–1,700), Kamado-ya for dango and donburi (¥300–1,400), Sumibiyaki Yamakujira for charcoal skewers (¥500–1,400), Shinanoya for amazake and warabimochi, Kyuyama for nikuman and kakigori. Between shows, the dango at Kamado-ya or a nikuman at Kyuyama are the only things you can eat standing. Brief the group in advance: these are Edo-period counters with no halal certification and sake on the menu.
x.mustBuy: Echigoya's "Sode-no-shita" (the bribe) manju box, ¥1,450 for nine — a joke gift where golden koban wafers are hidden under the buns so you can hand them over reciting the kabuki line. Nyanmage, the topknotted samurai-cat mascot, is the volume buy: steamed kintsuba ¥750 for nine, choco crunch ¥650 for ten, small plush from ¥1,500.
x.mustSee: The Oiran-douchuu courtesan procession — high-clogged oiran gliding down the main street with attendants, free with admission and the best photo of the day. Then stand on Nihonbashi looking down the street: 49.5 hectares of real timber Edo buildings, still used as a working film set.
x.confidenceNote: The 2026 admission price could not be confirmed — the official ticket pages are unreachable and the only figure retrievable was an older ¥4,800 one-day pass, against ¥5,800 quoted elsewhere with an ¥5,000 group rate for parties of 8+. Confirm before budgeting. Also, a standalone "koban chocolate" is not currently in the line-up despite older blog lists.

items.name: Hotel Nikko Tsukuba
items.subtitle: ホテル日航つくば
items.summary: Night 5, check-in 18:30 after a 123 km, 2h10 run — and dinner was already eaten at 17:15 en route, so this is a shopping-and-a-stroll evening, not a meal. Be honest with the group: an 11-storey city hotel in a 1970s planned science city, 285 m from Tsukuba Station. There is NO shop, NO bar and NO large bath in the building. The Subaru banquet hall is under renovation through September 2026.

essentials.detail: Saturday, and the retail window closes at 20:00. After that: Q't 3F for late food to 23:00, Starbucks in CREO to 23:00, and a 24-hour FamilyMart inside Q't 210 m from the lobby — which matters, because the hotel gives you nothing after 21:00. Anyone wanting a drink in-house must be in Sansui or Touri before last orders (20:30 and 19:30). Then the rocket walk: 600 m out through the park, back inside 40 minutes.

Breakfast at Restaurant Serena on 2F, 06:30–09:30 — but the hall seats only 70, so 35 people is half the room and a pre-set group section should be arranged. Nothing in Tsukuba's visitor economy opens before the 08:30 coach: JAXA 09:30, the Expo Center 09:50, the mall 10:00. The realistic option is a 06:30 walk into Tsukuba Chuo Park, unenclosed and always open, 470 m away — the pond, the modernist civic buildings, and haze permitting Mount Tsukuba's twin peaks closing the northern axis the city was planned around.

x.mustDo: Walk the 200 m to Tonarie Tsukuba Square — Q't, MOG and CREO, all shops closing at 20:00 — which makes the usable window about 85 minutes from an 18:30 arrival. Announce it on the coach before anyone unpacks. Then the 600 m loop through Tsukuba Chuo Park to the rocket.
x.mustEat: Ibaraki is Japan's undisputed natto capital, so put a plate of it on tomorrow's breakfast and let people try it — the group will not meet it again. Locally: Hitachi beef (served in-house at Sansui, 2F, last orders 20:00), Tsukuba-dori chicken, and Tsukuba ramen, a double pork-bone and seafood broth. After 20:00 the only kitchens near the hotel are on Q't 3F, which runs to 23:00; Saino, the Indian restaurant there, is the likeliest halal-friendly option, but phone rather than assume.
x.mustBuy: Tsukuba no Yoi Shina on B1 of Tsukuba Station, open until 20:00: Tsukuba ham and bacon, and the excellent fukure-mikan shichimi chilli blend — light, cheap, distinctive and perfect for taking back to Malaysia. Next door, Tsukuba City Bussankan carries the 46 certified Tsukuba Collection products. Ibaraki grows over 90% of Japan's hoshi-imo, so buy that too — honestly labelled: drying only starts in September, so a September shelf holds last winter's crop.
x.mustSee: The full-size 50-metre H-II rocket standing in the forecourt of the Tsukuba Expo Center, 600 m away — floodlit after dark, unfenced from the public path, and needing no ticket. It is the best photo in walking distance. Do NOT promise JAXA's Space Center: it is 2.2 km away and opens after your coach has left.
x.confidenceNote: One correction for anyone using older lists: LALA Garden Tsukuba no longer exists — it closed on 16 October 2022 and was demolished. Q't, MOG and CREO all still trade but the complex was rebranded Tonarie Tsukuba Square. Also unverified: the H-II rocket's nightly floodlight on/off times are not published anywhere.

x.summary: Up the Iroha-zaka hairpins first thing for the falls, then down to the shrine complex and across to the Edo theme park, and a long 123 km run to Tsukuba. Note the order: the falls come FIRST today, at 09:20, which is the one time of day Lake Chuzenji is genuinely cool — it sits at 1,269 m, where the September average low is 11.9°C, about 8°C below Tokyo. A light layer for the morning, not a fleece for the night.
x.sun: Sunrise 05:22, sunset 17:54. Kegon at 09:20 has the sun SE at az 127°, alt 45° — behind you at the basin platform, which is exactly right. By Toshogu at 11:00 it is SSE az 163°, alt 56°, near its harshest.
x.outfitPhoto: Toshogu is the hard one on this trip: gilded gold and vermilion carving in deep cedar shade, punched through by hard sunlit gaps at a 56° sun. That is a brutal dynamic range, and it punishes both extremes — white blows out in the lit patches, black dies in the shade. Wear a MID-TONE. Kegon is the opposite and the one place all week where warm colours win: grey rock, white water, green cliff, so rust, mustard or coral genuinely pop. At Edo Wonderland everyone around you is in Edo costume, so either rent one or wear plain solids; modern prints look wrong in every frame.
x.outfitPractical: The 09:20 Kegon stop is the single coolest hour of the trip — 1,269 m, roughly 17–19°C, with spray carrying about 150 m to the deck on a windy day, so a light layer AND the expectation of getting slightly damp. Toshogu is gravel and stone with 207 optional steps to the Okumiya; shoes stay on for the main route. Edo Wonderland is 49.5 hectares of gravel and timber, and costume rental takes 30–45 minutes to dress, which costs you a show.

legs.label: Day 5 by coach — Kinugawa up the Iroha-zaka to Kegon Falls (41 km, 50 min), down to Toshogu (16 km), across to Edo Wonderland (16 km), then 123 km and 2h10 southeast to Tsukuba

days.areaSpan: Tsukuba → Hitachi Seaside Park → Kawagoe → Shibuya → Shinjuku

items.name: Hitachi Seaside Park
items.subtitle: 国営ひたち海浜公園
items.summary: 09:30 — literally the opening bell, since the park runs 09:30–17:00 through 1 September to 31 October. The regular closing day in September is TUESDAY, not Monday, so Sunday 13 September is open. Admission ¥450 adult, ¥290 for groups of 20+, and the ¥350 seasonal surcharge does NOT apply in September.

x.mustDo: Enter at the West Gate and go straight up Miharashi Hill where the kochia are planted. With one hour and 215 hectares you cannot walk it — buy the Seaside Train one-day ticket at ¥600, or rental cycles at ¥600 adult. If two minutes can be spared, the big Ferris wheel gives the hill-and-ocean panorama in one shot.
x.mustEat: Ibaraki melon and hoshi-imo soft-serve from the West Gate kiosks — Hitachinaka and neighbouring Tokai produce the overwhelming majority of Japan's hoshi-imo, so this is genuinely local rather than generic. The Glass House café out in the dune area is the one place to sit with a full Pacific horizon.
x.mustBuy: Hoshi-imo — plain sliced, or the sweeter whole-dried maruboshi style — from the West Gate shop, and the green-kochia and nemophila merchandise (plush kochia balls, tins, towels) that is only sold here. Ibaraki melon IS genuinely in season: Earl's, the autumn melon, ships mid-July to late October and is the only Ibaraki melon available now.
x.mustSee: The GREEN kochia mounds on Miharashi Hill with the Pacific filling the frame behind them — shoot east from the summit path, then low into the sun for translucent lime-green. Pampas grass plumes near Pyonpyon Circle are just past their peak but still standing.
x.confidenceNote: Be straight with the group about the flowers: per the park's own calendar the kochia is green from mid-August to late September, turns red mid-October, and the ¥350 surcharge is charged only for about 20 days in October. Zinnia and sunflowers are finished and cosmos do not start until early October — mid-September is a genuine flower lull, and the app's "nemophila" line is months out. The 2026 Kochia Carnival dates were not yet posted.

items.name: Kawagoe Old Town (Kurazukuri Street)
items.subtitle: 川越 蔵造りの町並み
items.summary: 13:30–14:30 after a 150 km, 2-hour run. A Sunday afternoon is good timing — the shops are all open (most trade 10:00 to 17:00–18:00), unlike an early-morning slot that would find shutters down. Kawagoe Castle Honmaru Goten is closed Mondays, so today it is open, though one hour will not stretch to it.

x.mustDo: Walk the kurazukuri row north from Nakacho, using the 1918 former Eighty-Fifth Bank (now Saitama Resona Bank) as your landmark, then turn off to the Toki no Kane bell tower and on to Kashiya Yokocho — about 30 surviving penny-sweet shops, and one of Japan's official 100 Fragrant Landscapes since 2001. One hour is exactly the street and the sweet lane; do not add a museum.
x.mustEat: Kasho Umon's imo-koi eaten hot at the Toki no Kane shop — a yam-flour steamed bun around a slice of Kawagoe sweet potato and chestnut-azuki paste, and the most Kawagoe thing you can put in your hand. For a sit-down there is unagi at Ichinoya (founded 1832) or Ogakiku (founded 1807), though an hour makes that a stretch. Wash it down at Koedo Kurari with COEDO's Beniaka, the beer actually brewed with Kawagoe sweet potato.
x.mustBuy: Kurazukuri Honpo's Fukugura, a monaka packed with whole azuki and mochi, is the standard Kawagoe gift box. Add imo-senbei sweet-potato crackers from Kameya (founded 1783) and sweet-potato confections from Imoju, then in Kashiya Yokocho pick up Matsuriku Seika's metre-long fu-gashi and Tamariki Seika's hand-pulled candy — cheap, visual and perfect for 35 people.
x.mustSee: Toki no Kane itself: three tiers, about 16 m, rebuilt in 1894 after the Great Kawagoe Fire, one of Japan's 100 Soundscapes to be Preserved. It chimes at 06:00, 12:00, 15:00 and 18:00 — and a 13:30–14:30 slot misses the 15:00 by half an hour, so it is a photo rather than a sound. Osawa House (1792) is the oldest kurazukuri on the street and a National Important Cultural Property.
x.confidenceNote: Kawagoe Matsuri 2026 is 17–18 October, so there is no clash — you get the Edo streetscape rather than the million-visitor float parade, but equally no festival. The 2026 closing days and prices for Ogakiku and Ichinoya, and the Kikuya, Imoju and Koedo Kurari details, could not be confirmed from primary sources (koedo.or.jp, ogakiku.com and machikawa.co.jp all refused automated fetches).

items.name: Shibuya Scramble Crossing
items.subtitle: 渋谷スクランブル交差点
items.summary: 15:30–16:30, free, 24/7. A Sunday afternoon is the shopping-and-strolling crowd rather than the commuter surge — busy and photogenic, without the 3,000-people-per-light crush of a weekday evening. Good light, too, well before the 17:54 sunset.

x.mustDo: Cross it at least twice — once carried along by the wave pouring out of the Hachiko Exit, once from the opposite corner facing back — then get above it, because it only reads as a spectacle from height. Free vantage points are the Shibuya Scramble Square 2F walkway and the Tsutaya upper-floor windows; MAG'S PARK, the paid rooftop of MAGNET by SHIBUYA109, gives the straight-down shot.
x.mustEat: Nothing at the crossing itself — that is the honest answer, and street-eating in the middle of it is both impossible and frowned on. Walk two minutes to the Tokyu Food Show in Scramble Square's basement or the ShinQs food floors at Hikarie for bento, onigiri and famous-name sweets a group can buy fast and eat sitting down. Tonight's 17:00 dinner is an unagi grilled rice set, so keep appetites intact.
x.mustBuy: SHIBUYA109, the cylindrical tower on the Dogenzaka corner, is the landmark stop; Tokyu Food Show B2 is the better bet for edible gifts that survive a flight. Don Quijote Shibuya Honten, 24 hours and eight minutes away, is where a group clears a list fast.
x.mustSee: The stacked screens of the Tsutaya / QFRONT building are what makes the crossing photograph the way it does in films — stand with your back to Hachiko and shoot into them. Then find Taro Okamoto's enormous "Myth of Tomorrow" mural in the JR-to-Keio Inokashira passage, a genuinely major artwork most visitors walk straight past.

items.name: Shinjuku Granbell Hotel
items.subtitle: 新宿グランベルホテル
items.summary: Night 6, check-in 18:30 — and note this is the KABUKICHO Granbell, not the Shibuya one. It sits in the quieter north-east corner: 4 minutes to Higashi-Shinjuku Station, 6 to Golden Gai and Hanazono Shrine, 15 to JR Shinjuku. Dinner was at 17:00 elsewhere, so this is the trip's one genuinely free city evening.

essentials.detail: Sunday gives the full neon with less crush than a Friday. The Godzilla Head roars on the hour until 20:00 — leave by 19:45 for the last one. Golden Gai and Omoide Yokocho are open but with more shutters down. The honest caveat: touting is already illegal here, Shinjuku City designates Kabukicho a no-touting zone, and it is still worked on Ichibangai, Central Road, Kuyakusho-dori and Sakura-dori. The pattern is a ¥300–1,000 price advertised and a much larger bill delivered. Do not stop walking when approached, say "daijoubu desu" and keep going, only enter a bar you chose yourself with prices at the door, pay cash, never hand over a passport or card. Skip the Okubo Park stretch of Shokuan-dori after midnight. Last trains 00:20–00:45.

Breakfast is the 12F Restaurant G buffet, 07:00–10:30, in a glass-walled room over Shinjuku, so the 07:30 sitting is comfortable. Sunrise is 05:23 and the best dawn walk is the six minutes to Hanazono Shrine — ungated, open at any hour — looping back through Golden Gai's alleys while they are empty, swept and photogenic. Shinjuku Gyoen does NOT work: it opens 09:00, half an hour after the coach leaves, and Monday is its closing day.

x.mustDo: Take the Toei Oedo Line two stops from Higashi-Shinjuku to Tochomae — about 5 minutes, ¥180 — for the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building: a free 10-minute projection-mapping show on the building's face from Citizens' Plaza, then the free 45F South Observatory at 202 m, open to 22:00, last entry 21:30. One subway fare each, no cover charge, no touts, air conditioning, and back by 22:15. Better than any paid tower.
x.mustEat: Shinjuku Kabuki Hall on 2F of Tokyu Kabukicho Tower, 600 m away: about 1,300 seats across nine regional stalls, kiosk-fixed prices, no seating charge, open around the clock — the only place in Kabukicho that can absorb 35 people at any hour. For a solo late bowl, Ichiran on Shinjuku-dori is 24 hours with single-person booths. Both are pork-heavy; Kabuki Hall's Kanto, Kyushu-Okinawa and Korean stalls give the widest choice for anyone avoiding it.
x.mustBuy: Don Quijote Shinjuku Kabukicho, 600 m, 24 hours, with a tax-free counter needing a passport and ¥5,500 in one transaction. Matcha KitKat multipacks and Tokyo Banana are stacked near the entrance. In mid-September heat buy the chocolate last and put it straight in the room fridge.
x.mustSee: Their own 13F rooftop bar and terrace — 62 open-air seats looking down into the Kabukicho neon with the Metropolitan Government twin towers behind. The catch is the Sunday timetable: 14:00–22:30 instead of the 04:00 close it keeps the rest of the week, so go up before 21:00. The ¥500 table charge is waived for hotel guests, and reservations are guests-only, so just walk up.
x.confidenceNote: The rooftop bar's Sunday hours are the one loose end — the official site and Lets Enjoy Tokyo both give 14:00–22:30, but Gnavi still lists Sunday 17:00–23:30. Phone 03-5155-2412. Kabuki Hall's own site says 24 hours while the tower floor guide says 06:00 to 05:00; either way it is open at 01:00.

x.summary: The longest driving day: up to the Ibaraki coast, then 150 km back across to Saitama for the old merchant quarter, and into Tokyo. Two expectation-setters. The app's own summary calls Hitachi "seaside nemophila fields" — nemophila is a late-April to mid-May flower and there will be none. And the kochia there is solid summer GREEN in mid-September; the crimson is four to five weeks away.
x.sun: Sunrise 05:18, sunset 17:48 — the earliest sunset of the trip. Hitachi at 09:40 has the sun SE at az 135°, alt 48°; Kawagoe at 13:45 is SW az 231°, alt 46°; Shibuya at 15:45 is WSW az 256°, alt 24°.
x.outfitPhoto: The single best colour day of the trip, and it has one hard rule: DO NOT WEAR GREEN AT HITACHI. Miharashi Hill in September is tens of thousands of lime-green kochia domes under a blue sky with the Pacific behind — anything green makes you part of the shrubbery. White, cream, coral, red and yellow are spectacular against it. Kawagoe inverts the rule: the kurazukuri warehouses are BLACK-plastered clay, so black and charcoal vanish into the walls, and light colours pop hard. Shibuya at 15:45 is mixed LED colour, where plain solids beat busy patterns.
x.outfitPractical: Hitachi is the exposed bit: 215 hectares with no shade on a Pacific coast, strong sun at 48° and enough wind to take a hat off the back of your head. Then Kawagoe at 13:45 is the hottest hour of the whole trip — 30–31°C inland, on a treeless asphalt corridor with no shade at all. Between them is a 150 km, two-hour coach leg, and after Kawagoe another hour, so wear something you can sit in comfortably for three hours.

legs.label: Day 6 by coach — Tsukuba to Hitachi Seaside Park (74 km, 1h), then 150 km and 2h across to Kawagoe, 47 km and 1h down to Shibuya, and 5 km to Shinjuku

days.areaSpan: Shinjuku → Tokyo Tower → Tsukiji → Shisui → Narita

items.name: Tokyo Tower
items.subtitle: 東京タワー
items.summary: 09:00–10:30, arriving right at opening. Main Deck (150 m) runs 09:00–23:00, no closing days, so a Monday is fine — and a working Monday morning is the quietest kind. Admission ¥1,500 adult, the same online or at the counter, no timed reservation needed; the published group rate for 20–49 is ¥1,350, though the travel-agency schedule quotes ¥1,080, so have the agent confirm which applies. Coach parking is free while the group is on the deck if settled in one transaction.

x.mustDo: Main Deck only, and use the whole 90 minutes. Have the guide hold pre-issued group tickets and be at the Foot Town 1F lifts for the 09:00 opening — on a weekday morning the deck is close to empty and 35 people can spread out. Then work down: glass floor and the 360° circuit on Main Deck 1F, Tower Daijingu and the shop on 2F, out by 10:20. The Top Deck Tour does NOT fit: it is 40–60 minutes on its own, 90–120 door to door, reservation-only, and any group of 11+ must book through an agency.
x.mustEat: Cafe La Tour on Main Deck 1F does the Premium Tower Soft — soft serve with a monaka wafer printed with the Noppon Brothers, the tower's mascots — but it opens 09:30. For the group the halal-safer named pick is the halal-certified soft serve at Marion Crepes on Foot Town 1F, which opens at 09:00. Be warned the FOOT TOWN food court is effectively shut at that hour: Mos Burger and its Tokyo Tower Burger open 11:00, as does Siddique Palace on 2F.
x.mustBuy: TOKYO TOWER OFFICIAL SHOP THE SKY on Main Deck 2F, open from 09:00: the deck-exclusive Tower Daijingu goshuin at ¥300 and its omamori at ¥700, Tokyo Tower Caramel ¥280, the Nihon-Zanmai wooden magnet ¥600 which is the usual overseas-visitor pick, and mineral water in a tower-shaped bottle ¥410. If 35 people need more choice, the GALAXY shop on Foot Town 3F is wider and also opens 09:00.
x.mustSee: Three things. The Skywalk Window glass floor on Main Deck 1F, looking 145 m straight down — do it first, it jams once tour traffic arrives. Tower Daijingu on 2F, the highest shrine in Tokyo's 23 wards. And for the exterior group photo, the courtyard of Zojoji Temple 300 m southeast, shooting back at about 300° with the Daiden main hall in the foreground — at 09:00 the sun is behind the photographer, so hall and tower are both front-lit. Frame the Daiden, not the Sangedatsumon gate, which is inside a restoration shed until around 2032.
x.confidenceNote: Mt Fuji is unlikely and should not be promised: it sits about 98 km out at bearing 250°, and Tokyo's own observation record averages 2.9 visible days in September against 19.1 in January. Published tenant hours do shift — have the guide re-confirm the food and shop openings a week out. Note also that this stop replaces the Shibuya Sky pin that appeared on the Trip 1 map; the app is unambiguous that Trip 12 gets Tokyo Tower.

items.name: Tsukiji Outer Market
items.subtitle: 築地場外市場
items.summary: 10:50–11:50. Shops run roughly 05:00/06:00 to 14:00, closing Sundays, national holidays and sometimes Wednesdays — Monday is not a regular closing day and 14 September is not a holiday, so it is a FULL trading day. A Monday that IS a holiday, like 21 September, would be shut. The market's own rhythm is 06:00–09:00 trade and 09:00–14:00 public, so late morning is a good slot — busy but past the crush.

x.mustDo: Start at Namiyoke Inari Shrine, the market's guardian shrine with the giant lion heads and the tamago, sushi and prawn memorial stones, then work the 4-chome lanes back on foot. Brief the group hard: this is a stand-and-eat market with almost no seating, and you never carry raw fish onto the coach.
x.mustEat: Tsukiji Yamacho (06:00–15:30, open 365 days) for hot tamagoyaki on a skewer at roughly ¥150 — the one shop guaranteed open whatever the calendar says. Marutake and Shoro are the other tamagoyaki names, both Monday-open. Kitsuneya (06:30–13:30) does the hormone-don eaten standing at a plank counter for ¥1,000–1,200, and Sanokiya (07:00–15:00) sells the tuna-shaped cakes at about ¥250. Note today's 12:15 lunch is a crab miso set, so eat light.
x.mustBuy: Knives at Tsukiji Aritsugu (05:30–15:00) or Tsukiji Masamoto (06:00–15:00), with Sugimoto Hamono and the Tojiro Knife Gallery as friendlier-priced alternatives — all Monday-open. For matcha and nori, Maruyama Nori Honten (07:00–18:00) and its Kengo Kuma-designed tea salon Jugetsudo — and specifically NOT Uogashi Meicha, which closes Sundays AND Mondays. Katsuobushi, kombu and sealed nori from Ito Noriten travel home well.
x.mustSee: The turret trucks still nosing through the lanes are the market's signature moving image — Turret Coffee at 2-12-6 Tsukiji is named for them and has one parked inside. Overhead, the low tarpaulin roofs now sit directly against the cranes of the Tsukiji redevelopment: the best single frame of old and new Tokyo in the neighbourhood.

items.name: Shisui Premium Outlets
items.subtitle: 酒々井プレミアム・アウトレット
items.summary: 14:30–17:00, two and a half hours, after a 60 km run east. Open 10:00–20:00 March through January and it closes only one day a year, so Monday 14 September is open. Tax-free is still deducted AT THE TILL — passport to the cashier, ¥5,000 minimum per store per day — because Japan does not switch to airport refunds until 1 November 2026.

x.mustDo: Collect the floor map at the Information Center and split the 2.5 hours into two 70-minute halves with one hard regroup point — 220 units is far more than a group can browse coherently. Tell everyone to carry their passport in hand: exemption is granted shop by shop, not at a central desk.
x.mustEat: There is a food court and a restaurant row, and a mid-afternoon slot means this is the sensible coffee-and-sit stop rather than a meal — dinner is at the hotel at 18:00. Chiba is peanut country, so look for boiled and roasted rakkasei in the food shops; the boiled new-crop kind is genuinely in season right now.
x.mustBuy: The genuine draws are American accessible luxury and sportswear at deep outlet cuts — Coach, Michael Kors, Polo Ralph Lauren, Tommy Hilfiger, Nike, Adidas, New Balance, The North Face — where the yen price beats Kuala Lumpur retail badly. For things you can only get in Japan, target Onitsuka Tiger, Beams and United Arrows, and keep each shop's receipt separate to clear the ¥5,000 threshold per store.
x.mustSee: It is a flat, single-level, open-air American-village layout, so from the central plaza you can see the whole strip end to end — which is exactly why it works as a split-and-regroup coach stop. It sits about 20 minutes from Narita, so aircraft on the approach pass overhead all afternoon.
x.confidenceNote: A Shisui-specific overseas-visitor "Welcome Card" coupon could not be verified, nor the individual brand and food-court tenant list — the official English pages expose only hours, the 220-store count and the tax-free rules. Coordinates are approximate. It is open-air with little shade, so hold a wet-weather regroup point.

items.name: International Resort Hotel Yurakujo
items.subtitle: インターナショナルリゾートホテル 湯楽城
items.summary: Night 7, check-in 17:30, dinner 18:00. Mystery solved: the name is 湯楽城, not 有楽城, and this is the FORMER RADISSON NARITA — a 490-room 1978 property built by Delta Air Lines, bought by CHI Group in 2016 and renamed in September 2022. That is why it was unfindable before. Beyond the gate it is airport-belt farmland: 490 rooms in carrot and watermelon fields, nothing walkable.

essentials.detail: Monday, and the evening is on-site — which is fine, because the on-site thing is good. Say the quiet part out loud: the nearest konbini beyond the hotel is 1.4 km along an unlit rural road, so nobody should walk out. In practice the konbini IS the one in the lobby. Then the bath complex until 22:00, the Vista Lounge and SuperStars sports bar, and the indoor pool to 21:00. A free city shuttle runs to Keisei Narita and Aeon Mall Narita at 17:30, 18:30, 20:00 and 21:30 — but it is seats-only by law, so it cannot take 35 people at once.

Breakfast is 06:30 at the California Restaurant, which is its exact opening minute — the room seats 140 so capacity is fine, but throughput at minute one is not, so ask for a pre-set group section. Then the coach: the hotel says about 20 minutes to the airport against the app's 15, so budget 20–25 for a 10:55 flight. If anyone wants a dawn payoff, Sakura-no-Yama opens at 06:00 and Narita's night curfew lifts about then, so first light and the first arrivals coincide — but it only works as a deliberate stop written into the run to Terminal 1.

x.mustDo: Tokyo Yurakujo, the attached bath complex 100 m away in a converted Delta flight-catering factory — an Edo-townscape build with open-air baths, tub baths, a medicinal bath, sauna and stone-bed sauna. Hotel guests get a free entry voucher worth ¥1,800. Check the clock: today is a plain Monday, so its MONDAY hours apply — 17:00–22:00 rather than the 13:00 opening of every other day, last admission 21:00. Your 17:30 arrival lands right on it.
x.mustEat: Dinner is in-house at the California Restaurant, 1F, 140 seats — a buffet on a rotating international theme, and the hotel's Hawaiian Buffet runs 1 July to 30 September, so mid-September is inside it. The area's real dish is unagi on the Naritasan approach at Kawatoyo Honten, but that needs a daytime slot and phone booking for parties of ten or more.
x.mustBuy: There is a 7-Eleven inside the hotel lobby with Chiba souvenirs and an ATM, which for a group flying at 10:55 tomorrow is the most useful retail on the property. The proper local buy is peanut monaka from Nagomi no Yoneya on the Naritasan approach — peanut paste in a peanut-shaped wafer. Boiled peanuts (oomasari) are genuinely in season from early September; the roasted new crop is not out until mid-October.
x.mustSee: Aircraft, not scenery. The hotel sits 4.4 km from Narita Terminal 1 under the approach corridor. The named spot is Narita Sakura-no-Yama, about 4 km away — a grassed hill at the northern threshold of Runway A where landing aircraft pass low overhead, free, open 06:00–23:00, with three free large-coach bays.
x.confidenceNote: Identity, address, coordinates and the former-Radisson history are all now verified. Two things to correct: despite the 湯 in the name and the hotel's "large hot-spring spa" wording, the bath operator's own page states the water is NOT a hot spring, so do not sell it as an onsen. And the app's "free JR train ticket from your city station back to the hotel station" appears on no hotel or spa page — Tomisato has no railway station at all, so the ticket most likely means JR Narita Station, with the free shuttle or a taxi covering the last 8 km. Unverified: the lobby 7-Eleven's hours, and whether the city shuttle runs a reduced Monday service.

x.summary: The last full day: the tower at opening, the outer market at its tail end, then 60 km east for the outlets and out to Narita for the packing night. Monday 14 September is a normal working Monday and NOT a public holiday — which is exactly what you want, because Tsukiji Outer Market closes on Sundays and holidays, so today is a full trading day.
x.sun: Sunrise 05:23, sunset 17:50. At the 09:10 Zojoji group shot the sun is SE at az 125°, alt 43° — so shooting WNW toward the tower puts it squarely behind the photographer and front-lights every face. From the Main Deck at 09:40 (az 133°) Skytree to the NNE is front-lit, and anything SW is into the sun.
x.outfitPhoto: Tokyo Tower is INTERNATIONAL ORANGE and white, and that dictates the day: orange and red clothing fights the tower in every frame. White, navy, denim blue and black all read cleanly against the orange lattice and a September sky. Tsukiji is the opposite problem — its lanes are roofed in blue and green tarpaulin, which throws a cold cast over skin, so a warm-toned top quietly cancels it. If you want one exterior group photo of the whole trip that looks composed, the Zojoji courtyard at 09:10 is it.
x.outfitPractical: Tsukiji is the shoe decision: wet, fishy ground, narrow lanes, almost no seating, and stand-and-eat throughout — closed shoes you do not mind, and a small bag rather than a backpack you will swing into someone's display. Tokyo Tower's Main Deck has a glass floor you stand on, which is worth knowing if you are in a skirt. Shisui from 14:30 is flat, open-air and unshaded for two and a half hours.

legs.label: Day 7 by coach — Shinjuku to Tokyo Tower (10 km, 30 min), Tsukiji (4 km, 20 min), then 60 km and 1h10 east to Shisui, and 14 km on to Tomisato

items.name: Narita Airport — Terminal 1 South Wing
items.subtitle: 成田国際空港 第1ターミナル 南ウイング
items.summary: The Star Alliance terminal — Singapore Airlines check-in on 4F of the South Wing, gates via Satellite 3. The app shows no arrival time for this row, but a 06:30 breakfast and a 15–25 minute transfer puts you here around 07:15–07:45. The counter for a 10:55 departure opens roughly 08:00–08:25, and the landside omiyage streets from about 07:30. Terminal numbers are not printed in the app; T1 is inferred from Singapore Airlines' Star Alliance allocation.

x.mustDo: Do the souvenir run BEFORE security, not after. The 4F landside shopping street — Narita Nakamise, the airport's biggest concentration of Japanese sweets, typically 07:30–20:00 — is far better stocked than the airside satellites. Have every passport out: tax-free is still deducted at the till, so there is no refund counter, but each shop needs the passport or the Visit Japan Web code. Clear security by about 09:45.
x.mustEat: Eat before you fly. Terminal 1's landside 4F and 5F food floors are the place — a last bowl of ramen or a conveyor sushi counter, plus bento counters for anyone who wants a box for the gate. If you arrive before 07:30 the only thing trading is the 5F Capsule Marche gachapon shop (05:00–23:00) and the vending machines.
x.mustBuy: This is the heavy-and-chilled stop — do not carry these down from Tohoku. Tokyo Banana as the default office omiyage; ISHIYA Shiroi Koibito in 12/18/24-piece tins, which travel perfectly; ROYCE' Nama Chocolate LAST, with the ice pack, in hand baggage not the hold, because it is refrigerated; matcha and regional KitKat; Tokyo Fugetsudo Gaufre as the safest large box for sharing at the office. In the liquor hall, remember Malaysian customs allows 1 litre per adult.
x.mustSee: The free observation deck on 5F, looking straight down Runway A — the best way to burn 30 minutes of a long pre-flight wait, and the only place in the building where 35 people can spread out.
x.confidenceNote: Terminal assignment is solid (T1 South Wing is Star Alliance, and SQ637 was allocated Gate 33), but the individual shop names and floors are indicative rather than verified — the airport's shop finder is JavaScript-driven. Confirm the tenant list on arrival.

x.summary: Breakfast at 06:30, then a short coach to Narita. SQ637 departs Narita Terminal 1 at 10:55 and lands Singapore 16:55; a 2h15 connection, then SQ142 SIN 19:10 → Penang 20:35. You leave from Narita even though you arrived at Haneda. Welcome back to Penang.
x.sun: Sunrise 05:21, sunset 17:46 at Narita. At the 07:00 coach the sun is due E at az 100°, alt 19° — low, warm and straight down the runway axis if anyone is watching from the hotel side.
x.outfitPhoto: The last frames are the Terminal 1 group shot and whatever the 5F observation deck gives you. If the trip has a shirt or a company colour, today is the day to wear it — it is the one photo where 35 people are in one place, indoors, unhurried. Otherwise plain solids again.
x.outfitPractical: Breakfast at 06:30 is the restaurant's opening minute and the coach follows, so lay everything out the night before. Then twenty hours home: slip-on shoes, a light long-sleeve for two cabins, and compression socks for 8h25 of seat time. Weigh bags before you leave the room — 25 kg checked, 7 kg hand-carry, one piece, nothing over 32 kg.
